claims.text: Laser-assisted machining with laser preheating and a TiAlN/SH-coated end mill improves the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys relative to conventional machining.
The proposed intervention is laser-assisted machining with laser preheating and a TiAlN/SH-coated end mill.
Approximately 700°C is typical of high-temperature applications relevant to the proposed extreme environment.
The proposed performance boundary may include oxidizing atmospheres.
The machining intervention will reduce machining-induced surface damage.
The machining intervention will reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced surface damage and thermal gradients will produce a refined near-surface microstructure with finer grains.
Reduced surface damage and thermal gradients will lower near-surface residual stresses.
Laser preheating minimizes abrupt temperature gradients during machining.
The TiAlN/SH-coated end mill reduces mechanical adhesion during machining.
The TiAlN/SH-coated end mill reduces tool-induced damage.
A less damaged and more uniform microstructure with reduced residual stress will increase high-temperature yield strength.
A less damaged and more uniform microstructure with reduced residual stress will improve creep resistance.
At approximately 700°C, laser-assisted-machined specimens will have statistically significantly higher yield strength than conventionally machined specimens.
At approximately 700°C, laser-assisted-machined specimens will have statistically significantly better creep resistance than conventionally machined specimens.
The predicted improvement applies to high-entropy alloys manufactured by traditional synthesis methods before machining.
